title: Conversational backpressure and cost smoothing PRD
author: Hannah Lee
content:
Summary:
This PRD proposes a product and runtime feature called "Conversational Backpressure and Cost Smoothing" (CBCS). The feature aims to reduce customer unit cost volatility and mitigate transient capacity pressure for conversational workloads by applying coordinated, predictable throttling and graceful fidelity reduction at the session level while preserving latency SLOs and transparent billing signals.

Context and problem statement:
- Conversational workloads often exhibit "bursty" arrival patterns: short spikes of many parallel sessions followed by idle periods.
- Bursts drive up short-term provisioning (warm pools and preemptible capacity) and create tail latency incidents when real-time capacity is saturated.
- Existing fallback/fidelity systems (variant fallback, quantization fallback) operate after a request is accepted, and billing remains per-token — leading to cost surprises for customers and poor cost predictability for Redwood.
- Customers building transactional chat (support, checkout assistants) need predictable per-session economics, and platform teams need smoother capacity consumption curves for planning and pricing.

Primary goals (what success looks like):
1) Reduce peak per-tenant token spend variance by 30% for production conversational clients during observed burst events (measured over a 90-day window).
2) Reduce incidence of latency SLO violations caused by transient capacity saturation by 40% in staged customers.
3) Provide explicit controls and telemetry so customers can opt into session-level smoothing with clear billing implications (no surprises).
4) Launch a developer-facing API and Console controls + an SDK helper to make adoption low-friction.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting core serving kernels or model architecture changes (this is an orchestration/runtime policy layer).
- Long-term pricing model redesign (only introduces a controlled crediting/discount primitive for smoothed sessions).

Target customers and personas:
- Mid-market SaaS product engineering teams facing bursty conversational traffic (ticketing systems, finance chatbots).
- Platform teams managing tenant costs and enforcing per-route budgets.
- Solution engineers and SREs running Dedicated/Private deployments wanting deterministic capacity profiles.

Key product features and requirements (high-level):
- Session backpressure policy: ability to define a per-tenant (or per-route) smoothing window (e.g., 30s, 2m) and a max concurrent active-token-rate for in-flight sessions.
- Graceful fidelity ladder: declarative fidelity reduction steps (e.g., full LLM -> quantized variant -> short prompt summary -> failure) applied per-session with configured thresholds.
- Admission control and queuing: short-lived admission queues that hold requests for < configurable ms (default 200ms) before applying fidelity ladder or rejecting.
- Billing primitives: a smoothed-session credit model that converts accepted queued time into token-credit discounts and logs transparent cost adjustments.
- Visibility: Console-level session economics dashboard, per-session trace IDs, and telemetry export to ingestion pipelines.
- Developer-facing API/SDK: client-side helper that surfaces estimated wait time, applied fidelity, and preflight checks.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile token latency must not exceed existing per-route SLO by more than 20ms for admitted requests.
- Cost telemetry latency: cost and credit events must appear in Console within 60s of request completion.
- Security/compliance: all session-level telemetry must honor PII redaction and existing VPC/customer-data controls (no payloads stored by default).

Detailed behaviors and examples:
- Example policy YAML (customer-facing declarative snippet):
  policy_name: session_smoothing_preset_1
  smoothing_window_ms: "30000"
  max_concurrent_tokens_per_tenant: "4000"
  queue_timeout_ms: "200"
  fidelity_ladder: ["gpt-large-int8","gpt-medium-int8","summary-short"]
  billing:
    smoothing_credit_ratio: "0.25"  # server grants 25% credit on token charges for queued time up to smoothing_window
  rollout:
    mode: gradual
    canary_percent: "10"

- Runtime flow (succinct):
  1. Request arrives at front door with route+tenant metadata and session id.
  2. Router computes tenant's current token rate; if above threshold, request is placed into a short-lived FIFO wait queue (<= queue_timeout_ms).
  3. If slot becomes available within timeout, request is admitted at requested fidelity; otherwise server attempts next fidelity in ladder and retries admission.
  4. If all ladder steps fail, the system returns a structured fallback response (reason=backpressure, suggested_retry_ms) and applies no smoothing credit.
  5. Billing system emits 2 events: raw_usage_event (tokens, fidelity) and smoothing_credit_event (credit_amount, reason).

API and SDK changes (developer experience):
- New API param: smoothing_policy_id (string) on chat/generate endpoints. Default: null (opt-out).
- Response additions: header X-Smoothing-Applied: true/false and JSON body field "smoothing": {"applied":true, "fidelity":"gpt-medium-int8", "queue_ms":45, "credit_applied":12}.
- Client SDK helper (JS/Go): will preflight a "shouldQueue" check and surface estimated queue time and potential credit to the application UI.

Console and observability:
- New Console view: Session Smoothing -> per-tenant timeline with: queued-ms percentile, applied-fidelity histogram, smoothing-credit spent, and SLO impact heatmap.
- Telemetry events and metrics: smoothing.queue_time_ms, smoothing.admit_rate, smoothing.fidelity_switch_count, smoothing.credit_issued_total
- Alerts: create an SRE alert if smoothing.admit_rate drops below 80% of expected during canary window or if smoothing.credit_issued_total grows > 2x baseline in 1h.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal alpha (2 weeks)
   - Implement policy primitives and runtime queue. Tests: synthetic burst harness. Internal-only console flags.
   - Owners: runtime eng (Marcus Chen), product (Hannah Lee), applied-ml (Priya).
2) Customer canary (6 weeks)
   - Identify 3 customers across Hosted and Dedicated. Nightly canary runs with 10% of traffic routed through CBCS.
   - Monitor: 99p latency, smoothing.credit_issued, customer cost-feedback survey.
   - Thresholds to proceed: reduce token variance by >=20% for canary tenants and no increase in error rate.
3) Gradual rollout (8 weeks)
   - Enable self-serve in Console for +50 customers. Offer guidance and defaults.
   - Release SDK helpers and sample UI components.
4) GA and docs (2 weeks)
   - Publish public docs, pricing FAQ and billing contract amendment templates for enterprise.

Rollout steps (detailed numbered checklist):
1. Merge runtime admission control changes behind feature flag.
2. Add smoothing_policy storage and SDK to the Console config store.
3. Add telemetry hooks and event schemas to the ingestion pipeline.
4. Perform synthetic burst load tests and perf regression tests on the runtime.
5. Run internal alpha, capture metrics and iterate.
6. Invite canary customers, instrument SDK, and run for 6 weeks.
7. Evaluate canary metrics and PRD success targets, update pricing credit rules.
8. Ship to self-serve and publish docs.

Billing and pricing implications:
- Smoothed sessions will be eligible for a configurable smoothing_credit_ratio. Credits are informational on invoices and applied as a line-item adjustment.
- For Dedicated customers, smoothing may be disabled by default unless enabled by account team (due to contractual reserved capacity semantics).
- Internal cost model: estimate smoothing reduces peak provisioned warm capacity by enabling short queues rather than immediate instance spin-ups. We will run cost simulations against historical traces to quantify.

SLOs and success metrics (measurable):
| Metric | Baseline | Target (90 days) | Measurement window | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Tenant token spend variance (p95/p5) during bursts | TBD (measure in alpha) | -30% | 90d rolling | Product |
| 99p token latency | route baseline | <= baseline + 20ms | Canary window | Eng SRE |
| Smoothing adoption rate (opt-in %) | 0% | >25% of eligible customers | 12 weeks post GA | Go-to-market |
| Number of SLO incidents attributed to transient saturation | baseline | -40% | 90d | Eng SRE |

Operational readiness and runbook highlights:
- Runbook for increased queue_time_ms: check smoothing.admit_rate, fallback fidelity switch counts, and recent capacity changes. Consider temporary policy relax (increase max_concurrent_tokens_per_tenant) or burst-provision.
- Failure modes and mitigation:
  1) Telemetry lag: fall back to sampling logs and alert customers.
  2) Large fidelity regression: automatically pause smoothing for affected tenant and open a rollback.
  3) Billing mismatches: reconcile raw_usage_event and smoothing_credit_event via offline job and fix invoice pipeline.

Open questions and risks:
- Pricing & contract risk: enterprise legal may require clearer warranty language around smoothing credits; need finance input on liability exposure.
- UX clarity: how to present queued delays to end-users without degrading perceived responsiveness? (Suggested: show typing indicators and estimated wait).
- Timing of Dedicated opt-in: Dedicated customers often expect zero surprises; need well-documented SKUs and explicit sales opt-in.

Dependencies and owners:

- Billing events and invoice line items: Finance & Billing (owner: Laura Gomez from finance-legal)
- Console UX and SDKs: Developer Experience (owner: Diego Ortega)

{
  "id": "msg_abc123",
  "smoothing": {
    "applied": true,
    "policy_id": "session_smoothing_preset_1",
    "fidelity": "gpt-medium-int8",
    "queue_ms": 78,
    "credit_applied": 18
  },
  "choices": [ ... ]
}

Next steps:
- Approve PRD and schedule a cross-functional kickoff (runtime, billing, console, applied-ml, sales).
- Instrument initial metrics collection on synthetic and historical traces to compute baseline variance within two weeks.
- Prepare customer-facing FAQ and billing language for canary invites.
